```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", dev = "png",
                      fig.retina = 1.5, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.6,
                      fig.align = "center")
library(mlvtoolbox)
has_jpeg <- requireNamespace("jpeg", quietly = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = has_jpeg)
# Drawing helpers. Every panel is a canvas in image coordinates (x rightward,
# y downward, pixel centres at integers), so stages line up like the pages of
# a flip-book.
canvas <- function(xlim, ylim, main = NULL) {
  plot.new()
  plot.window(xlim + c(-0.5, 0.5), rev(ylim) + c(0.5, -0.5), asp = 1,
              xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")
  if (!is.null(main)) title(main = main, cex.main = 1, font.main = 1, line = 0.5)
}
paint <- function(colours, xlim, ylim) {
  rasterImage(as.raster(colours[ylim[1]:ylim[2], xlim[1]:xlim[2], drop = FALSE]),
              xlim[1] - 0.5, ylim[2] + 0.5, xlim[2] + 0.5, ylim[1] - 0.5,
              interpolate = FALSE)
  rect(xlim[1] - 0.5, ylim[2] + 0.5, xlim[2] + 0.5, ylim[1] - 0.5, border = "grey70", lwd = 0.5)
}
grey_of <- function(v, faint = 0) {
  v <- pmin(pmax(v, 0), 1); v <- faint + (1 - faint) * v
  matrix(grDevices::grey(v), nrow(v), ncol(v))
}
# Signed values on a diverging palette, blue below zero and red above,
# symmetric about zero.
diverging <- function(v, limit) {
  pal <- grDevices::hcl.colors(101, "Blue-Red 3")
  k <- 51 + round(50 * pmin(pmax(v / limit, -1), 1))
  matrix(pal[k], nrow(v), ncol(v))
}
contour_length <- function(d) vapply(d$contours, function(z)
  sum(sqrt(rowSums((z[, 3:4, drop = FALSE] - z[, 1:2, drop = FALSE])^2))), 0)
draw_contours <- function(d, lwd = 0.9, col = "black")
  for (z in d$contours) segments(z[, 1], z[, 2], z[, 3], z[, 4], lwd = lwd, col = col)
# Number of 8-connected groups of TRUE pixels in a logical matrix.
count_groups <- function(m) {
  lab <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(m), ncol(m)); lab[m] <- which(m)
  repeat {
    old <- lab
    for (dr in -1:1) for (dc in -1:1) {
      sh <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(m), ncol(m))
      rr <- max(1, 1 + dr):min(nrow(m), nrow(m) + dr); cc <- max(1, 1 + dc):min(ncol(m), ncol(m) + dc)
      sh[rr - dr, cc - dc] <- lab[rr, cc]
      lab <- pmin(lab, sh, na.rm = TRUE); lab[!m] <- NA
    }
    if (identical(lab, old)) break
  }
  length(unique(lab[m]))
}
```

To measure a photograph or a painting, you first need its line drawing. The
Mid-Level Vision (MLV) Toolbox traces photographs with learned models
(structured edges or the Segment Anything model). `mlvtoolbox` bundles no
model weights; `trace_rgb()` takes the extractor as a `backend` function and
records it with the drawing. This vignette describes the package's own
extractor, which needs no weights, `extract_lines()`, and its backend form,
`xdog_lines()`:

```{r quick, eval = FALSE}
img <- read_mlv_image("painting.jpg")
drawing <- trace_rgb(img, backend = xdog_lines)
```

The extractor aims to follow the image's form (outlines, folds and major
shading boundaries) rather than individual brush strokes, places each line on
its edge to within about a pixel, and is deterministic. It is a filter, not a
model. Each stage is a published image operation, except a small step of this
package's own that places lines on the edges and draws thin strokes once, and
all ten parameters are recorded with the result.

```{r no-jpeg, include = !has_jpeg, eval = !has_jpeg, results = "asis"}
cat("The rest of this vignette reads a JPEG image and needs the suggested",
    "package 'jpeg', which is not installed.\n")
knitr::knit_exit()
```

## The running example

```{r example, include = FALSE}
painting <- system.file("extdata", "melendez-still-life.jpg", package = "mlvtoolbox")
img <- read_mlv_image(painting)
h <- dim(img)[1]; w <- dim(img)[2]
stages <- line_extraction_stages(img)
drawing <- trace_rgb(img, backend = xdog_lines)
stopifnot(identical(trace_contours(stages$mask)$contours, drawing$contours))
```

The example is Luis Meléndez's *Still Life with Fish, Bread, and Kettle*
(c. 1772, oil on canvas; The Cleveland Museum of Art, accession 1983.97), a
public-domain painting released under Creative Commons Zero (CC0) through the
museum's Open Access programme. The package includes it downsampled to
`r w` × `r h` pixels (`r round(file.size(painting) / 1024)` KB);
`inst/extdata/README.md` gives its source and licence. That is the width at
which the defaults were tuned.

```{r fig-showcase, echo = FALSE, fig.retina = 1.5, fig.height = 2.75, fig.cap = sprintf("The painting (left) and its drawing at the default settings (right): %d contours, %.0f px of line, %d of them shorter than 15 px. The arc of the round copper vessel behind the fish, the fish's head, the loaves, the citrus fruit and the table edge are recognisable; the pewter vessel at right, dark on a dark wall, is broken into pieces, and the wall's streaks and the fish's scales leave many short marks.", length(drawing$contours), sum(contour_length(drawing)), sum(contour_length(drawing) < 15))}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 1.6, 0.2))
canvas(c(1, w), c(1, h), "Painting")
paint(as.raster(img), c(1, w), c(1, h))
canvas(c(1, w), c(1, h), "Traced drawing")
rect(0.5, h + 0.5, w + 0.5, 0.5, border = "grey70", lwd = 0.5)
draw_contours(drawing, lwd = 1)
```

```{r read}
painting <- system.file("extdata", "melendez-still-life.jpg", package = "mlvtoolbox")
img <- read_mlv_image(painting)
dim(img)
drawing <- trace_rgb(img, backend = xdog_lines)
drawing
```

## Stage by stage

`line_extraction_stages()` runs the same computation as `extract_lines()` and
returns every intermediate image. The figures below show them for the fish's
head, numbered as the steps are taken, on the same canvas, so they can be
compared like the pages of a flip-book.

```{r crop, include = FALSE}
cx <- c(200, 386); cy <- c(27, 174)
win <- function(m) m[cy[1]:cy[2], cx[1]:cx[2]]
changed <- mean(abs(win(stages$smoothed) - win(stages$lightness)) > 0.02)
anis <- win(stages$flow$anisotropy)
# Stages 4a and 4b share one diverging scale, saturating at a third of the
# largest |DoG| in the image.
dog_limit <- max(abs(stages$dog)) / 3
clipped <- mean(abs(win(stages$dog)) > dog_limit)
patches_dog <- count_groups(win(stages$dog) < 0)
patches_response <- count_groups(win(stages$response) < 0)
band_px <- sum(win(stages$band)); mask_px <- sum(win(stages$mask))
# The painting is dark, so both lightness panels share one stretched grey
# scale: the window's 1st to 99th percentile of lightness, black to white.
lim <- unname(quantile(win(stages$lightness), c(0.01, 0.99)))
stretch <- function(v) (v - lim[1]) / diff(lim)
```

**Lightness.** The image is converted from sRGB to CIE L\* lightness (white
is 100), divided by 100. Lightness is close to perceived brightness, so equal
steps are about equally visible across the range. With `colour = TRUE` the
next two stages also use the colour axes a\* and b\*; the line decision itself
always uses lightness.

```{r stage-lightness, echo = FALSE, fig.retina = 1.5, fig.cap = sprintf("Stage 1. Brushwork is finer than form: the head's scales are speckled and the copper vessel behind it is mottled, both finer than the outlines the drawing should keep. CIE lightness of the fish's head, on a grey scale stretched from L* = %.0f (black) to %.0f (white), the window's 1st and 99th percentiles.", 100 * lim[1], 100 * lim[2])}
par(mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 1.6, 0.2))
canvas(cx, cy, "1  Lightness")
paint(grey_of(stretch(stages$lightness)), cx, cy)
```

**Pre-filter.** An anisotropic Kuwahara filter (Kyprianidis, Kang and
Döllner 2009) replaces each pixel with the mean of the most uniform part of an
elliptical neighbourhood, aligned with the local edge and split into eight
overlapping sectors. Within a region it averages away texture; at a boundary,
the uniform sectors lie on one side, so the boundary stays sharp. `smooth`
sets the radius, here `r stages$extraction$parameters$smooth` px.

```{r stage-smoothed, echo = FALSE, fig.retina = 1.5, fig.cap = sprintf("Stage 2. The pre-filter flattens texture but not outlines: the scales and the mottling merge into flat patches while the head, eye and gill stay sharp. Kuwahara radius %g px; %.0f%% of the window's pixels changed by more than 2 L* units. Grey scale as in Stage 1.", stages$extraction$parameters$smooth, 100 * changed)}
par(mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 1.6, 0.2))
canvas(cx, cy, "2  Pre-filtered")
paint(grey_of(stretch(stages$smoothed)), cx, cy)
```

**Edge tangent flow.** The structure tensor of the smoothed image, the local
average of the gradient's outer product at scale `sigma_c`, gives at every
pixel the direction along which lightness changes least: the edge tangent
(Kyprianidis and Döllner 2008). Its anisotropy, from 0 to 1, says how clearly
one direction dominates.

```{r stage-flow, echo = FALSE, dev = "jpeg", fig.ext = "jpg", dev.args = list(quality = 90), fig.cap = sprintf("Stage 3. The tangents ring the eye and run along the outlines of the head; in the background they follow faint streaks and turn from patch to patch. Blue segments at every fifth pixel over the faded pre-filtered image, 1 to 5 px long as the anisotropy rises from 0 to 1 (median %.2f here).", median(anis))}
par(mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 1.6, 0.2))
canvas(cx, cy, "3  Edge tangent flow")
paint(grey_of(stretch(stages$smoothed), faint = 0.55), cx, cy)
gx <- seq(cx[1] + 2, cx[2] - 2, by = 5); gy <- seq(cy[1] + 2, cy[2] - 2, by = 5)
pts <- expand.grid(x = gx, y = gy)
tx <- stages$flow$x[cbind(pts$y, pts$x)]; ty <- stages$flow$y[cbind(pts$y, pts$x)]
len <- 0.5 + 2 * stages$flow$anisotropy[cbind(pts$y, pts$x)]
segments(pts$x - len * tx, pts$y - len * ty, pts$x + len * tx, pts$y + len * ty,
         col = "#0072B2", lwd = 1.1)
```

**Flow-based difference of Gaussians.** At every pixel a one-dimensional
difference of Gaussians, `G_sigma - tau * G_(k sigma)`, is taken across the
flow (Kang, Lee and Chui 2007). It is negative on the dark side of an edge and
positive on the light side. With `tau` just below 1, a uniform area keeps a
small positive value, so faint texture does not cross zero.

```{r stage-dog, echo = FALSE, fig.retina = 1.5, fig.cap = sprintf("Stage 4a. Each outline becomes a pair of bands, blue on its dark side and red on its light side; the background's remaining texture gives weak, broken responses. Difference of Gaussians across the flow (sigma = %g px, k = %g, tau = %g), blue below zero, red above, saturating at +/- %.3f, a third of the image's largest value (%.0f%% of this window is clipped).", stages$extraction$parameters$sigma, stages$extraction$parameters$k, stages$extraction$parameters$tau, dog_limit, 100 * clipped)}
par(mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 1.6, 0.2))
canvas(cx, cy, "4a  Difference of Gaussians")
paint(diverging(stages$dog, dog_limit), cx, cy)
```

The response is then averaged along the flow, over a Gaussian of scale
`sigma_m` following each tangent streamline. Along an outline the averaging
adds up responses of the same sign and joins short gaps; across texture it
mixes signs and cancels. A streamline stops once it has turned more than 20
degrees from where it started, so corners are not rounded off.

```{r stage-response, echo = FALSE, fig.retina = 1.5, fig.cap = sprintf("Stage 4b. Averaging along the flow (sigma_m = %g px) joins the blue bands and thins the background speckle: the window's separate blue patches fall from %d to %d. Palette as in Stage 4a. The blue, where the response is below eps = %g, is the ink band of Stage 5.", stages$extraction$parameters$sigma_m, patches_dog, patches_response, stages$extraction$parameters$eps)}
stopifnot(patches_response < patches_dog)
par(mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 1.6, 0.2))
canvas(cx, cy, "4b  Averaged along the flow")
paint(diverging(stages$response, dog_limit), cx, cy)
```

**Threshold and placement.** The XDoG threshold (Winnemöller, Kyprianidis
and Olsen 2012) turns the response into an ink band, and the band lies on
the dark side of each edge, about 1.2 `sigma` deep. A drawing traced from the
band would sit beside the edges. The next step is this package's own: each
line is drawn on the boundary between the band and its light side, at the
pixel nearer the edge. A thin stroke is drawn once, along its middle: a dark
band no wider than 3 `sigma` with light on both sides, or a narrower light gap
(up to about 4 px at the default `sigma`) with dark on both sides. Groups of line pixels smaller than `min_component`
pixels are removed.

```{r stage-mask, echo = FALSE, fig.retina = 1.5, fig.cap = sprintf("Stage 5. The lines (black, %d px) run along the light-side edge of the ink band (pale blue, %d px), where the lightness changes, not through its middle. Isolated band patches in the background are outlined too, unless the outline has fewer than min_component = %d pixels.", mask_px, band_px, stages$extraction$parameters$min_component)}
par(mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 1.6, 0.2))
canvas(cx, cy, "5  Band and lines")
paint(ifelse(stages$mask, "black", ifelse(stages$band, "#C6D4EE", "white")), cx, cy)
```

`trace_contours()`, which `trace_rgb()` calls, then thins the mask to one
pixel and traces it into contours, splitting them where lines meet.

```{r stage-traced, echo = FALSE, dev = "jpeg", fig.ext = "jpg", dev.args = list(quality = 90), fig.cap = sprintf("Stage 6. Each contour runs along the boundary it came from rather than beside it: the outline of the head, the pupil and the curves of the gill are each one or a few contours. Traced contours (black; %d touch this window) over the faded painting. The lines are pixel chains; simplify in trace_contours() turns them into fewer, straighter segments.", sum(vapply(drawing$contours, function(z) any(z[, 1] >= cx[1] & z[, 1] <= cx[2] & z[, 2] >= cy[1] & z[, 2] <= cy[2]), TRUE)))}
par(mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 1.6, 0.2))
canvas(cx, cy, "6  Traced contours")
faint <- img; for (k in 1:3) faint[, , k] <- 0.45 + 0.55 * img[, , k]
paint(as.raster(faint), cx, cy)
clip(cx[1] - 0.5, cx[2] + 0.5, cy[1] - 0.5, cy[2] + 0.5)
for (z in drawing$contours) segments(z[, 1], z[, 2], z[, 3], z[, 4], lwd = 1.4)
```

## How the parameters change the drawing

Two parameters do most of the work. `sigma` sets the scale of the edges that
are drawn: small values follow fine detail, large values only broad
boundaries. `smooth` sets the radius of the pre-filter: 0 turns it off and
draws texture.

```{r sweep, include = FALSE}
sweep <- expand.grid(sigma = c(1, 2, 3), smooth = c(0, 3, 5))
sweep$traced <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(sweep)), function(i)
  trace_contours(extract_lines(img, sigma = sweep$sigma[i], smooth = sweep$smooth[i])))
sweep$contours <- vapply(sweep$traced, function(d) length(d$contours), 0L)
sweep$median <- vapply(sweep$traced, function(d) median(contour_length(d)), 0)
corner_median <- function(sg, sm) sweep$median[sweep$sigma == sg & sweep$smooth == sm]
sweep$short <- vapply(sweep$traced, function(d) sum(contour_length(d) < 15), 0L)
# The caption's claims, kept to effects far larger than the small pixel
# differences between JPEG decoders: each step up in sigma loses lines in
# every row, and from sigma = 1 to 2 the median grows; at sigma = 1 smoothing cuts the count several
# fold. Neighbouring panels at sigma = 3 differ too little to rank reliably.
cnt <- matrix(sweep$contours, 3, dimnames = list(sigma = c(1, 2, 3), smooth = c(0, 3, 5)))
med <- matrix(sweep$median, 3, dimnames = dimnames(cnt))
stopifnot(all(cnt[2, ] < 0.85 * cnt[1, ]), all(cnt[3, ] < 0.85 * cnt[2, ]),
          all(med[2, ] > 1.1 * med[1, ]),
          cnt[1, 3] < 0.5 * cnt[1, 1], med[3, 3] > 3 * med[1, 1])
```

```{r fig-sweep, echo = FALSE, fig.retina = 1.5, fig.height = 5.2, fig.cap = sprintf("Larger sigma gives fewer lines in every row; smoothing matters most at sigma = 1 (%d contours unsmoothed, %d at smooth = 5) and little at sigma = 3. Columns: sigma = 1, 2, 3 px; rows: smooth = 0, 3, 5 px; the default is bottom middle. The median contour grows from %.0f px (top left) to %.0f px (bottom right).", cnt[1, 1], cnt[1, 3], corner_median(1, 0), corner_median(3, 5))}
par(mfrow = c(3, 3), mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 1.4, 0.2), oma = c(0, 1.8, 1.4, 0), xpd = NA)
for (i in order(sweep$smooth, sweep$sigma)) {
  canvas(c(1, w), c(1, h), sprintf("%d contours", sweep$contours[i]))
  if (sweep$smooth[i] == 0) mtext(sprintf("sigma = %g", sweep$sigma[i]), side = 3, line = 1.5, cex = 0.85, font = 2)
  if (sweep$sigma[i] == 1) mtext(sprintf("smooth = %g", sweep$smooth[i]), side = 2, line = 0.5, cex = 0.85, font = 2, las = 0)
  rect(0.5, h + 0.5, w + 0.5, 0.5, border = "grey70", lwd = 0.5)
  draw_contours(sweep$traced[[i]], lwd = 0.5)
}
```

The defaults (`sigma = 2`, `smooth = 5`, `tau = 0.98`, `sigma_m = 3`,
`min_component = 20`) were chosen by eye on four public-domain paintings
640 px wide, this one among them: two still lifes with crisp outlines in dark rooms, a
landscape built of thick directional strokes, and a landscape of broad colour
fields. They are a judgment, not an optimum. `sigma`, `sigma_c`, `sigma_m` and
`smooth` are in pixels, so an image twice as large wants them about twice as
large.

## Measuring the drawing

A traced drawing is an ordinary `mlv_drawing`, so every measure in the package
applies to it. Per-contour features:

```{r features}
features <- feature_table(drawing)
dim(features)
round(head(features[, c("orientation_1", "orientation_5", "length_4", "curvature_1")], 3), 3)
```

```{r features-check, include = FALSE}
junctions <- detect_junctions(drawing)
mat <- analyse_mat(drawing, properties = "parallelism")
halves <- split_contours(mat$drawing, property = "parallelism", fraction = 0.5)
n_top <- length(halves$top$contours); n_bottom <- length(halves$bottom$contours)
len_top <- sum(contour_length(halves$top)); len_bottom <- sum(contour_length(halves$bottom))
n_unassigned <- length(halves$unassigned$contours); len_unassigned <- sum(contour_length(halves$unassigned))
n_unranked <- length(halves$unranked)
# Each contour's mean parallelism: the mapped scores at its pixel centres
# (traced vertices lie on pixel centres).
mapped <- mat$drawing$mat_images$parallelism
scores <- vapply(mat$drawing$contours, function(z) {
  v <- mapped[cbind(c(z[, 2], z[nrow(z), 4]), c(z[, 1], z[nrow(z), 3]))]
  if (any(is.finite(v))) mean(v, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_
}, 0)
```

Junctions are few for so many contours (`r nrow(junctions)`): most outlines in
the painting fade out rather than meet another line.

```{r junctions}
junctions <- detect_junctions(drawing)
table(junctions$type)
```

The medial axis describes the space between the lines. Parallelism is high
where two lines run alongside each other at a constant distance, such as the
stripes of the fish's body or the sides of the pewter vessel:

```{r mat}
mat <- analyse_mat(drawing, properties = "parallelism")
```

```{r fig-parallelism, echo = FALSE, fig.retina = 1.5, fig.height = 3.9, fig.cap = sprintf("Each contour coloured by its mean parallelism, the mean of the scores mapped onto its pixels (Viridis, 0 to 1; median over contours %.2f%s). Lines that run beside another at a steady distance, such as the stripes of the fish's body, score near the top; outlines facing open space, such as the arc of the copper vessel, score lower.", median(scores, na.rm = TRUE), if (any(is.na(scores))) sprintf("; %d contours without a score in grey", sum(is.na(scores))) else "")}
layout(matrix(1:2), heights = c(1, lcm(1.6)))
par(mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 1.6, 0.2))
canvas(c(1, w), c(1, h), "Parallelism")
rect(0.5, h + 0.5, w + 0.5, 0.5, border = "grey70", lwd = 0.5)
pal <- grDevices::hcl.colors(101, "Viridis")
for (k in seq_along(mat$drawing$contours)) {
  sc <- scores[k]; z <- mat$drawing$contours[[k]]
  segments(z[, 1], z[, 2], z[, 3], z[, 4], lwd = 1.6,
           col = if (is.na(sc)) "grey70" else pal[1 + round(100 * min(max(sc, 0), 1))])
}
par(mar = c(1.6, 6, 0.3, 6))
plot.new(); plot.window(c(0, 1), c(0, 1), xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")
rasterImage(as.raster(matrix(pal, 1)), 0, 0.35, 1, 1)
axis(1, at = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1), labels = c("0", "0.25", "0.5", "0.75", "1"), cex.axis = 0.8,
     mgp = c(1, 0.3, 0), tcl = -0.2)
```

Measurements can also select contours. Here the drawing is split by mean
parallelism into two halves of at most equal total length. The split does not
follow objects; it separates lines that run beside another line from lines
that face open space.

```{r split}
halves <- split_contours(mat$drawing, property = "parallelism", fraction = 0.5)
c(top = length(halves$top$contours), bottom = length(halves$bottom$contours))
```

```{r fig-split, echo = FALSE, fig.retina = 1.5, fig.height = 2.75, fig.cap = paste0(sprintf("The more parallel half of the drawing (left: %d contours, %.0f px) and the less parallel half (right: %d contours, %.0f px), each holding at most half the total length. ", n_top, len_top, n_bottom, len_bottom), if (n_unassigned - n_unranked > 0) sprintf("%s (%.0f px), ranked near the middle, would overflow either budget and belong%s to neither. ", if (n_unassigned - n_unranked == 1) "1 contour" else sprintf("%d contours", n_unassigned - n_unranked), len_unassigned, if (n_unassigned - n_unranked == 1) "s" else ""), if (n_unranked > 0) sprintf("%d without a score cannot be ranked. ", n_unranked), "Compare the stripes of the fish's body (left) with the arc of the copper vessel (right).")}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(0.2, 0.2, 1.6, 0.2))
for (part in list(list(halves$top, "More parallel"), list(halves$bottom, "Less parallel"))) {
  canvas(c(1, w), c(1, h), part[[2]])
  rect(0.5, h + 0.5, w + 0.5, 0.5, border = "grey70", lwd = 0.5)
  draw_contours(part[[1]], lwd = 0.8)
}
```

## Recording the extraction

The mask carries its definition, and `trace_rgb()` copies it into the
drawing, so a drawing states how it was made:

```{r provenance}
drawing$source$provider_version
str(drawing$source$extraction_parameters[c("sigma", "smooth", "tau")])
```

A feature specification can fix the extraction as well as the measures.
`trace_rgb()` then passes the specification's parameters to the backend and
checks that the mask it returns was made with them; a specification naming
another version of the extractor is rejected.

```{r spec}
spec <- feature_spec(extraction = list(lines = list(sigma = 2, smooth = 5)))
spec$definitions[["lines"]]
same <- trace_rgb(img, backend = xdog_lines, spec = spec)
identical(same$contours, drawing$contours)
try(feature_spec(extraction = list(provider = "xdog_lines", provider_version = "fdog-xdog-0")))
```

## Using a learned extractor

A learned edge or contour model fits the same slot. A backend is any function
that takes the RGB array and returns a logical ink mask of the same size; if
it attaches an `"extraction"` attribute, `trace_rgb()` records its version
and parameters. The package bundles no model weights, so the model, its
weights and its preprocessing remain the backend's responsibility. A sketch,
with a hypothetical `predict_edges()` that returns edge probabilities:

```{r learned, eval = FALSE}
model_lines <- function(image, threshold = 0.5) {
  probability <- predict_edges(image)          # your model, your weights
  mask <- probability > threshold
  attr(mask, "extraction") <- list(method = "my-edge-model-2024-06",
                                   parameters = list(threshold = threshold))
  mask
}
drawing <- trace_rgb(img, backend = model_lines, threshold = 0.4)
spec <- feature_spec(extraction = list(provider = "model_lines",
                                       provider_version = "my-edge-model-2024-06"))
```

The same mechanism works for any function. Here a threshold on lightness
stands in for a model: it marks the darkest twentieth of the painting as ink,
which is only useful for showing the provenance it records.

```{r toy-backend}
dark_lines <- function(image, fraction = 0.05) {
  lightness <- line_extraction_stages(image, smooth = 0)$lightness
  mask <- lightness < quantile(lightness, fraction)
  attr(mask, "extraction") <- list(method = "darkest-fraction-1",
                                   parameters = list(fraction = fraction))
  mask
}
toy <- trace_rgb(img, backend = dark_lines)
toy$source[c("extraction_provider", "provider_version", "extraction_parameters")]
```

## Limits

- Lines are decided on lightness. A boundary between two colours of equal
  lightness is not drawn, with or without `colour = TRUE`, which only lets
  colour steer the flow and the pre-filter.
- The pre-filter rounds sharp corners slightly: at the default radius a
  square's traced corner lies up to about 1.2 px inside the true corner.
- It also removes dark strokes narrower than about 2 px unless they lie along
  a pixel row or column; light strokes survive from 1 px. `smooth = 0` keeps
  them, so use it for thin line art.
- Parallel dark strokes 2 to 4 px apart (hatching) merge and are drawn as the
  pair's two outer outlines, with no line between them.
- Lines are placed to the nearest pixel. On synthetic edges the traced
  contours lie within 1 px of the true boundary (about 0.5 px on straight
  edges away from the image border), and a traced disc has the right length
  to within 2% after `simplify = 1`.
- All scales are in pixels. The defaults were tuned on four paintings 640 px
  wide; images of other sizes want `sigma`, `sigma_c`, `sigma_m` and `smooth`
  scaled with them.
